facts: The Trial Court, vide its judgment of conviction dated 5th November, 2003 and order of sentence dated 10th November, 2003, held all the five accused, namely, Sunil Kumar, Satish, Pawan Kumar, Jitender Kumar and Ratti Ram guilty of the offence under Section 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
The Trial Court further held that except Jitender, remaining four accused were also guilty of the offence u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC.
Chadan Singh, resident of Bhartana had eight children, two sons and six daughters.
Indra, the deceased, was having a son aged about two years from this marriage.
Ratti Ram had obtained a loan on his own land and purchased a tractor for the children of his sister-in-law (sali).
Satish and Sunil, along with Pawan, had also taken the cattle and other household articles from the house of Ratti Ram with his permission.
Indra had protested against Ratti Ram not bringing the cattle and household articles to their house.
On 9th February, 1999, Ishwar Singh, PW-11 had gone to the house of his sister Indra.
At night, after taking meals, all these guests slept on the ground floor, Surender went to irrigate the fields while Indra along with her son, went to sleep in the chobara.
When he went up to the chobara, he saw that Ratti Ram and his son Pawan Kumar had caught hold of the hands of Indra while Satish and Sunil were pulling the rope that had been put around her neck.
issues: Whether Jitender Kumar was correctly convicted for the offence under Section 120-B IPC.
Whether the delay in lodging the FIR is fatal to the case of the prosecution.
Whether the alleged recovery of the motorcycle Exhibit P44 is admissible in evidence.
petitioner_arguments: He has not been named in the FIR (Exhibit P2), which fact itself shows that he has been falsely implicated in the crime.

The occurrence is alleged to have taken place between 1.00 to 1.30 a.m. on 10th February, 1999 but the FIR has been registered after undue and unexplained delay, i.e., at 4.30 p.m. on 10th February, 1999.
The learned Trial Court as well as the High Court have misread and failed to appreciate the evidence in accordance with law.
The alleged recovery of the motorcycle Exhibit P44 is in furtherance to the statement of Jitender (Exhibit P43).
Accused Jitender had no motive to be involved in the crime and no role has been attributed to him so as to warrant his conviction for an offence u/s. 302 IPC.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution examined as many as 13 witnesses in support of its case and also produced documentary evidence including the report from the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL).

After putting up the evidence against the accused, their statements were recorded u/s. 313 CrPC and then, as already noticed, they were convicted by the Trial Court and their conviction has been upheld by the High Court also.
court_reasoning: The law is well-settled that merely because an accused has not been named in the FIR would not necessarily result in his acquittal.
The delay in lodging the FIR is fatal to the case of the prosecution in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
The alleged recovery of the motorcycle Exhibit P44 is admissible in evidence.
holding: We uphold the conviction of Jitender Kumar for the offence under Section 120-B IPC.
